answer: A trust atlas counters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to bind cryptographic identities to physical secure enclaves. Adversaries must expend verifiable capital acquiring discrete microchips rather than spawning free virtual instances. Enclave status updates propagate peer-to-peer across a whisper gossip network. However, hardware side-channel attacks remain a critical limitation, as credentials extracted from a compromised hardware relic can forge valid agent attestations until globally revoked.
